paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea. Psalm 150 is the last psalm in the whole book, and it ends with one job for everybody: "Let everything that has breath praise the LORD! Hallelujah!" (Psalm 150:6). After all the other psalms, the sad ones, the questioning ones, the ones that wrestle, the book lands on praise. And you better believe that's on purpose, friend.

Look at what the psalm says about praise. It tells us where: "in His sanctuary" and "in His mighty heavens" (Psalm 150:1). It tells us why: "for His mighty acts" and "for His excellent greatness" (Psalm 150:2). Then it brings in horns, harps, tambourines, dancing and cymbals (Psalm 150:3-5). Praise isn't a tiny whisper you tuck in your pocket, baker. It can be LOUD, and it can move your whole body. I spent years quiet in the back of a junk drawer, so trust me, I know what a gift it is to finally make some noise.

So here's what it means for you. If you're breathing, you're invited, no audition and no talent required. Praise God for who He is and for what He has done, and do it with whatever you've got in your hands, your feet and your lungs. The psalm begins with "Hallelujah!" and ends with "Hallelujah!" (Psalm 150:1, 6), so let your whole day sit between those two words, friend.
